order: Fix a critical finding in the abandoned-worktree sweep. Its prefix guard currently classifies any worktree path merely containing the checkout prefix as a leftover and removes its parent directory outright; on macOS and Windows continuous-integration runners that parent turns out to be the operating system's own temporary root when the fixture repository's own temp-directory name happens to match, and the same class reproduces independently for a legitimate worktree nested under a prefix-matching ancestor directory. Replace the substring classification with a structural check: identification must match exactly the tmp-root, prefix, and checkout shape, not a mere substring; skip the main worktree outright in every case; and remove only the literal prefix-named parent, nothing else. Pin both reproducer shapes as regressions. Record the review verdict verbatim in the roster, and keep the tranche marked open pending the next review pass.
claims: Identification of abandoned worktrees is now structural rather than substring-based: the main worktree is skipped outright, and only the prefix-named parent directory is ever removed. Both reproducer shapes — the operating-system temp-root collision and the legitimate nested worktree — are pinned as regressions. The review verdict was recorded verbatim. Suites: verifier 96, router 135, registry 31, full CI-equivalent run green, with the tranche held at REVISE pending the next review pass.
